question: What is the minimum attendance required to appear for the end-semester examination?
answer: A student must have a minimum of 75 per cent attendance in each course (computed separately for the theory and practical components) to be eligible to appear for the end-semester examination in that course. Attendance is calculated from the first day of instruction of the semester to the last instructional day and covers all lectures, tutorials and practical sessions.

question: How are marks split between internal assessment and the end-semester exam for a theory course?
answer: For a theory course, evaluation is split out of 100 marks: 40 marks are for continuous internal assessment and 60 marks for the end-semester examination conducted by the Controller of Examinations.

question: What is the minimum I need to score to pass a course?
answer: To pass a course you must secure at least 30% of the marks in the end-semester examination AND at least 40% of the total marks (internal assessment plus end-semester examination combined). Failing either condition will result in a grade of "F" in that course.

question: What letter grade do I get for 85 marks?
answer: Based on the grading table in AR §6.1, 85 marks out of 100 fall in the range 80 to 89, which corresponds to the letter grade A+ (Excellent) with 9 grade points.

question: How many days do I have to apply for re-evaluation after results are declared?
answer: You must apply for re-evaluation to the Controller of Examinations within ten working days of the declaration of results, on payment of the prescribed fee per course. No application shall be entertained after this period.

question: What happens if I miss an end-semester exam because I was ill?
answer: If you miss an end-semester exam due to illness, you must submit a medical certificate issued by a registered medical practitioner and countersigned by the Institute Medical Officer to the Controller of Examinations within five working days of the date of the examination. On acceptance of the certificate, you will be permitted to appear for the course in the next supplementary examination, and that appearance will be treated as your first attempt and you will be exempt from the supplementary examination fee.

question: What is the penalty if I am caught with a mobile phone in the exam hall?
answer: If you are caught with a mobile phone in the exam hall, it is treated as a first offence of using unfair means: the examination in that course will be cancelled and you will be awarded the grade F in that course. Mobile phones are explicitly listed as a prohibited item in the exam hall, and possession (whether used or not) counts as use of unfair means.

question: What time do the hostel gates close at night?
answer: The hostel gates close at 10:30 p.m. every day, and they open again at 5:30 a.m.

question: Can I use an induction cooktop in my hostel room?
answer: No. The use of induction cooktops in hostel rooms is prohibited. Any such appliance will be confiscated and a fine of Rs. 1,000 will be imposed for each occurrence.

question: How much is the late fee if I pay my semester fees after the due date?
answer: If you pay your semester fees after the due date, a late fee of Rs. 100 per day is charged, up to and including the last date shown in the schedule. The late fee for any single payment is capped at Rs. 1,500. Note that no payment is accepted after the last date, so the late fee only applies during the window between the due date and the last date.

question: What is the last date to pay the odd semester tuition fee?
answer: The last date to pay the odd semester tuition, examination and development fee is 31 July 2026. Payments made after this date are not accepted, unless the Registrar grants an exception for a documented delay in an education loan or scholarship disbursement, in which case the late fee applies up to the date of payment.

question: Who is eligible for the merit-cum-means scholarship?
answer: You are eligible for the Merit-cum-Means Scholarship if your annual family income from all sources does not exceed Rs. 3,00,000 and you have either a CGPA of at least 7.0 at the end of the preceding academic year or, if you are a first-year student, at least 80 per cent marks in the qualifying examination. Your application must be accompanied by an income certificate issued by a Tehsildar or an officer of equivalent rank, not older than six months.

question: Do I get leave if there is a death in my family?
answer: Yes. Under the bereavement leave policy, if a parent, sibling, grandparent or spouse dies, you are entitled to up to seven days of bereavement leave, which is counted as attendance. You must inform the HoD by e-mail or through the student portal before or during the leave, and submit a written application on return.

question: Will I get my hall ticket if I have not paid my tuition fees?
answer: No, you will not be issued a hall ticket if you have outstanding tuition fee dues on the last date of payment, and you will not be permitted to appear for the end-semester examination. However, your hall ticket shall be released within one working day of the dues being cleared, provided the examination has not yet commenced.

question: How long can a break of study be?
answer: A break of study may be granted for one semester or one academic year, but only on medical grounds certified by the Institute Medical Officer and approved by the Dean, and it cannot be granted more than once during the B.Tech. programme.

question: What is the maximum time allowed to complete the B.Tech programme?
answer: A student must complete all requirements of the B.Tech. programme within a maximum period of seven academic years from the date of first admission. Failure to do so will result in the student's name being removed from the rolls of the Institute.

question: Can I get a mess rebate if I go home for two weeks?
answer: Yes, you are entitled to a mess rebate for a two-week absence from the hostel. Under HH §4.3, a resident absent for a continuous period of seven days or more is entitled to a rebate of mess charges for the period of absence, provided the absence is recorded in the leave register in advance and the rebate form is submitted within seven days of your return. No rebate is admissible for absences of less than seven days, so your two-week stay at home qualifies.

question: How much medical insurance cover do students have?
answer: Every student is covered under the group medical insurance scheme of the Institute for hospitalisation expenses of up to Rs. 1,00,000 per year. The premium is included in the development fee, and claims are made through the Institute Medical Officer within thirty days of discharge from the hospital.

question: My attendance is 58% because I was hospitalised for three weeks. Can the shortage be condoned?
answer: The rulebook contradicts itself on this point. Clause 1 (AR §4.3) sets the minimum attendance for condonation at 65 per cent and states that below 65 per cent it 'shall not be condoned under any circumstances,' whereas Clause 2 (LM §2.2) sets the minimum at 55 per cent. These are incompatible thresholds for the same situation (medical condonation by the Dean). (Found by the corpus-wide audit, confidence 0.97.) Read on its own, AR §4.3 would give: No, your shortage of attendance cannot be condoned. Under AR §4.3, a shortage of attendance may be condoned by the Dean on medical grounds only if your attendance in the course is not less than 65 per cent. Since your attendance is 58 per cent, which is below 65 per cent, the rule expressly states that 'a shortage of attendance below 65 per cent shall not be condoned under any circumstances.' Additionally, for any future medical leave, please ensure you comply with the hospitalisation intimation requirement in LM §2.3 (informing the HoD and Dean through the Institute Medical Officer within three days of admission).

question: What is the lowest attendance percentage that can still be condoned on medical grounds?
answer: The rulebook contains two incompatible thresholds for condonation on medical grounds. AR §4.3 states that attendance must be 'not less than 65 per cent' and that a shortage 'below 65 per cent shall not be condoned under any circumstances.' LM §2.2, by contrast, permits condonation where attendance 'is not less than 55 per cent.' These provisions disagree on the very question asked, so the applicable minimum cannot be determined from the passages alone.

question: If I withdraw my admission before classes begin, how much of my tuition fee will be refunded?
answer: Two passages give incompatible figures for refunding the tuition fee when a student withdraws before the commencement of classes. SF §6.2 states that the tuition fee shall be refunded after deducting a processing charge of ten per cent of the tuition fee (i.e., 90 per cent refunded). FS §4.1 states that 100 per cent of the tuition fee shall be refunded if the withdrawal request is made before the commencement of classes. These clauses disagree on the very amount you asked about, so I cannot reconcile them.

question: What CGPA do I need to maintain to keep my merit scholarship?
answer: Two passages give different minimum CGPA thresholds for continuing your Merit Scholarship into the next academic year. AR §11.2 says you must maintain a CGPA of not less than 7.5 at the end of each semester, while SF §3.1 says the Merit Scholarship continues only if you maintain a CGPA of not less than 8.0 at the end of each semester. Both also state that falling below the threshold in any semester forfeits the scholarship for the rest of that academic year. The rulebook itself does not indicate which of these thresholds governs your case.

question: What happens if I miss the end-semester exam because of a family wedding?
answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if you miss an end-semester exam because of a family wedding. The closest passage covers absence from an end-semester examination on medical grounds only, not on personal or family grounds.

question: Can I get a re-test if I missed a mid-term test for a job interview?
answer: The rulebook does not address this situation. The closest clause covers a related case: You would not need a re-test. Under the Leave and Medical Policy, a student attending a placement interview arranged through the Institute's Training and Placement Cell shall be marked present for the duration of the interview or test, on production of the call letter countersigned by the Placement Officer. The re-test provision in the Examination and Evaluation Regulations applies only when a mid-term test is missed on medical grounds with a medical certificate submitted to the HoD within five working days, not for job interviews.

question: Can I change my branch after the first year?
answer: The rulebook does not address changing your branch (academic department) after the first year. The closest related provisions concern room changes within the hostel and adding/dropping individual courses, not branch transfers.

question: Is there a dress code for laboratory sessions?
answer: The rulebook does not address a dress code for laboratory sessions. The closest passage covers the requirement to submit a certified laboratory record in order to be admitted to the end-semester practical examination.

question: Can a day scholar eat in the hostel mess by paying per meal?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a day scholar can eat in the hostel mess by paying per meal. The closest passage covers the related rule that every resident must be a compulsory member of the hostel mess.

question: Are pets allowed in the hostel?
answer: The Hostel Handbook does not address whether residents may keep pets in the hostel. The closest passage it does cover is HH §5.4, which lists specific prohibited activities and items such as gambling, loud music, firecrackers, and overnight guests, but says nothing about animals.

question: What is the fee for a duplicate identity card?
answer: The rulebook does not address the fee for a duplicate identity card. The closest passage mentions the Institute identity card only in connection with examination-hall entry and permitted materials.

answer: The rulebook does not address whether a summer internship can earn academic credit. The closest related provision, Hostel Handbook §7.1, merely mentions that the Warden may permit a student to stay in the hostel for an internship, but it says nothing about awarding academic credits for one.

question: Is there a scholarship for students from the EWS category?
answer: The rulebook does not address scholarships specifically for students from the EWS (Economically Weaker Section) category. The closest passage covers the Merit-cum-Means Scholarship, which is available to students whose annual family income does not exceed Rs. 3,00,000, subject to CGPA/marks criteria.

question: Are grace marks given if I fail a course by one or two marks?
answer: The rulebook does not address grace marks for students who fail a course by one or two marks. The closest provision, AR §5.4, simply states the passing requirements — at least 30 per cent in the end-semester examination and at least 40 per cent of total marks — and says that failing either results in an 'F' grade, with no mention of any grace-mark provision.

question: Can I write my answers in Hindi instead of English in the end-semester exam?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether answers may be written in Hindi instead of English in the end-semester examination. None of the passages supplied deal with the language of answer scripts.

question: What happens if there is a printing error in the question paper?
answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if there is a printing error in the question paper. The closest related provision is EE §6.2, which only covers the correction of clerical errors in declared results by the Controller of Examinations within sixty days.

question: How do I get a duplicate degree certificate if I lose the original?
answer: The rulebook does not address the procedure for obtaining a duplicate degree certificate if the original is lost. The closest passage covers only when the original degree certificate is issued, not how to replace it.

question: Is there a fee concession if my sibling also studies at the institute?
answer: The rulebook does not address a fee concession on the basis of a sibling studying at the Institute. The closest passage it does cover is the concession granted to children of permanent Institute employees.

question: What is the minimum CGPA to be eligible for campus placements?
answer: The rulebook does not address the minimum CGPA required for eligibility for campus placements. The closest passage sets a CGPA threshold of 7.5 for continuation of the Merit Scholarship.

question: Can I re-appear in a course I have already passed to improve my grade?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student may re-appear in a course they have already passed in order to improve their grade. The closest passage, AR §5.4, only specifies the minimum marks required to pass a course and does not mention any provision for re-taking a course that has already been passed.

question: What happens if I fall ill in the middle of writing an exam?
answer: The rulebook does not address this situation. The closest clause covers a related case: If you fall ill while writing an exam, the rulebook does not specifically describe what happens during the exam itself, but it does address missed examinations on medical grounds. Under EE §3.3, if you miss a mid-term test due to illness and submit a medical certificate to the HoD within five working days, you must be given a re-test within two weeks of rejoining classes; the re-test is of the same standard and duration and is set by the course instructor. If your illness is serious enough to keep you out of more than half the instructional days of the semester, LM §2.4 says you should apply for a break of study with certification from the Institute Medical Officer.

answer: The rulebook does not address whether you may audit a course without earning credits. The closest passage defines a course as one 'carrying a specified number of credits' and requires registration for credit-bearing courses, but it does not mention auditing or non-credit participation.
